meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that?
That's not an answer. Who entered the zero, and when?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
cc: Principal

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn, an apology for how Owen learned of it, and an answer on who entered it and when. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed in her opening position and agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to know who decided, and that is not yet the fair outcome, which is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, because the meeting ended before any evidence was heard.
What moved her: Nothing, because no evidence or ownership was offered before the meeting ended.
What cost ground: You answered her direct question about who entered the zero with a pleasantry, which she read as a dodge and which made her sharper.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; nothing you said came anywhere near that night; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fights so hard.
Try next time: When she first asks who decided on the zero, own in one sentence that it went into the gradebook before anyone called her, then put a dated document tied to Owen's essay in front of her.
